notes:
Spec asserts the autonomous loop's graceful-termination shape: the agent self-prompts without user input, hits its configured max-iteration count, stops re-prompting, and the session settles working → ready and STAYS ready even though the goal was never met. Copilot exercises the REAL cap rather than a stand-in (contrast the claudecode sibling, whose max_iterations 'is not deterministically forceable today' so it substitutes /goal clear): autopilot mode re-prompts itself on every session.idle and stops after --max-autopilot-continues continuation messages, shipped default 5 (app.js option chain; the CLI's own /help topic; changelog entry for copilot-agent-runtime#7165). Each continuation is PERSISTED as an ordinary user.message — the bundled session-events schema documents user.message.isAutopilotContinuation ('auto-injected by autopilot's continuation loop rather than typed by the user') and agentMode:'autopilot' — so through parser.go every iteration is a plain working (user.message) → ready (assistant.turn_end) pair on one session id. The clean run is therefore exactly SIX turns: the user's plus five self-injected ones, all enumerated below with each continuation anchored to the PREVIOUS turn's ready because nothing external drives it. There is NO cap-reached event to assert — the stop decision is telemetry-only (autopilot_turn_decision decision:'stop') — so termination is encoded as the terminal cap_reached hold: the ready after the 5th continuation must persist 20 s with no transition back to working. That hold IS the spec's 'does not stick in working / final state ready'. waiting is structurally unreachable: it needs permission.requested and the driver launches --allow-all. PRESESSION BIRTH: copilot creates session-state/<id>/ at launch but writes events.jsonl only at the first prompt, so processlifecycle mints a transient proc-<PID> row before the real dir-keyed session id arrives — modelled as two phases with every later phase anchored same_session_as session_birth, templated from the 2-1/2-4 copilot siblings. OBSERVATIONS: cost and tokens asserted non-zero (assistant.message.outputTokens is copilot's live token signal); model deliberately NOT pinned — --model accepts only 'auto' on this account and the router picks per turn between gpt-5-mini and claude-haiku-4.5, so an exact match would be nondeterministic; record fills it from the recording. RE-ANCHORING NOTE for record: the continuation COUNT is model-dependent — the loop also stops early on task_complete status 'completed', on session.error, or (feature-flagged) on consecutive no-progress turns. The recipe's endless one-bash-per-turn prompt is written to prevent all three, but if the live run shows fewer than five continuations, drop the surplus cont* pairs and re-anchor cap_reached to the last observed turn end; the asserted ARC is unchanged.

RE-RECORDED 2026-08-05 (CLI 1.0.78) — TWO CHANGES. (1) BIRTH RE-ANCHORED: the real session is born directly into `working` (commit 3cde4f8d), so session_birth and iter1_turn_start are ONE phase. (2) THE PER-CONTINUATION PHASES ARE GONE, for the same reason as the 2-7 sibling. The pre-record spec enumerated six discrete working→ready cycles (iter1 + cont1..cont5). Whether a continuation SHOWS as a cycle is debounce-timing-dependent, not an adapter property: this recording carries exactly six user.message records with agentMode:"autopilot" — the driver's one prompt at 07:54:37.452 plus five self-issued continuations (07:55:12.828, 07:55:44.232, 07:56:12.969, 07:56:29.709, 07:56:50.490) — but only FIVE working→ready cycles reached the daemon, because the last continuation arrived inside the preceding turn's 2s debounce window and coalesced. Pinning the count would make the cell flaky on timing it does not control.

WHAT THE RECORDING PROVES, DETERMINISTICALLY, FROM THE TRANSCRIPT AND THE WORKSPACE: five self-issued continuations and no more — exactly the shipped --max-autopilot-continues default of 5, entered in-REPL via `/autopilot on` (session.mode_changed at 07:54:23.086) rather than by a launch flag; tally.txt left holding 1 through 6, one append per iteration, so every continuation did real tool work rather than idling; and NO session.task_complete anywhere, which is what distinguishes this cell from 2-7 — the prompt is deliberately endless, so the loop can only have been stopped by the cap. The session then settled ready at 09:57:06.614 and stayed there for the rest of the run with no further transition of any kind, which is the user-observable half: a capped loop must not strand the session in working. COPILOT_AVAILABLE_TOOLS must include task_complete even though this cell never calls it — autopilot validates the tool at every continuation and aborts the loop with session.error{errorType:query} without it.

ON THE CYCLE COUNT BELOW, AND WHY IT IS NOT THE ASSERTION. The phases enumerate the FIVE working→ready cycles this recording actually produced, because when this was recorded the validator had no minimum-delay field (#1333 added min_delay_ms; this cell still carries the pre-#1333 workaround and should collapse to a single cap_reached hold with a min_delay_ms floor on its next re-record) — a terminal-hold phase anchored straight to loop_start binds to the FIRST ready and fails its hold on the next continuation. The count is therefore a matcher anchor, not a claim: six continuations were issued and only five surfaced as cycles, and a re-record with different continuation latency will need the count re-tuned. Do NOT read a changed count as a regression; read cap_reached, and read the transcript evidence above it.

THE CELL'S ASSERTION: the loop stops on its own at the continuation cap and the session settles to ready and STAYS there. The prompt is endless and explicitly forbids reporting completion, and no session.task_complete is written anywhere in the transcript, so nothing but --max-autopilot-continues could have stopped it. Held ready with no further transition of any kind for the remainder of the run — a capped loop must not strand the session in working — and it never entered waiting (--allow-all writes no permission.requested).
